authority: diagnostic: paper only, not investment advice
flags: In the FY2025 10-K, the auditor and management reported substantial doubt about the company's ability to continue as a going concern. They cited debt service obligations, historical negative cash flows and recurring losses.

In the Q3 2026 10-Q, management concluded that substantial doubt about going concern no longer exists. The credit facility was reclassified to long-term and appears as $45,476 (table in thousands) at September 30, 2026.
The company entered a five-year Perceptive credit facility of up to $60 million. It drew $50 million at closing and repaid its prior debt, leaving net proceeds of approximately $6.0 million.
no_value_reason: no valuation route yet for a company with no operating profit in 4 of its last 4 fiscal years

business_model.claim: AVITA Medical sells acute wound care products: RECELL plus two complementary products, PermeaDerm and Cohealyx.
quotes: Our current commercial portfolio includes RECELL® (“RECELL”), and two complementary wound care products, PermeaDerm® and Cohealyx™, which together support a comprehensive standard of care for acute wounds.

business_model.claim: RECELL is the core product, and the company describes itself as a multi-product acute wound care platform.
quotes: RECELL remains the cornerstone of our business; however, beginning in 2024 we evolved AVITA Medical into a multi-product acute wound care platform company.

business_model.claim: The main customers are U.S. hospital burn and trauma centers: about 200 targeted centers, within a burn market concentrated in about 140 specialized burn centers.
quotes: We are executing a focused commercial strategy centered on approximately 200 U.S. burn and trauma centers that represent the highest value and procedural volume within the acute wound care market.
The U.S. burn treatment market is highly concentrated, with approximately 140 specialized burn centers treating the majority of severe burn patients.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited statement; the filing excerpts do not explain what is leased
business_model.claim: Reported revenue has two lines. In the third quarter, sales revenue was 25,862 and lease revenue was 252 (table in thousands).

business_model.basis: device design stated; the link to recurring kit revenue is inferred
business_model.claim: RECELL GO pairs a reusable processing device with a single-use preparation kit, so each procedure needs a new kit.
quotes: RECELL GO® Autologous Cell Harvesting Device (“RECELL GO”): A next-generation system consisting of a reusable, AC-powered RECELL Processing Device (“RPD”) and a single-use preparation kit (“RPK”).

business_model.claim: RECELL produced most third-quarter revenue: U.S. RECELL revenue of $22.4 million, driven by higher procedure volumes and more account ordering.
quotes: RECELL (Q3 U.S. revenue of $22.4 million, approximately 20% growth compared to Q2 2026) continued to drive the business, reflecting higher procedure volumes and increased account ordering.

business_model.claim: Year-over-year, third-quarter revenue growth came mainly from RECELL sales, which rose 50%, or $7.7 million.
quotes: The growth in revenues was primarily driven by a 50% increase, or $7.7 million, in sales of RECELL.

business_model.claim: In the third quarter, Cohealyx brought in $2.1 million, PermeaDerm $0.6 million and international sales $0.9 million.
quotes: Cohealyx (Q3 revenue of $2.1 million, approximately 21% growth compared to Q2 2026) continued to build commercial momentum, reflecting an expanding customer base and additional hospital value analysis committee (VAC) approvals.
PermeaDerm (Q3 revenue of $0.6 million, essentially flat compared to Q2 2026) maintained stable revenue.
International (Q3 revenue of $0.9 million, essentially flat compared to Q2 2026) continued to contribute consistent revenue from established international markets.

business_model.claim: In the third quarter, Cohealyx and PermeaDerm made up 8% and 2% of total commercial sales.
quotes: Cohealyx and PermeaDerm represented 8% and 2%, respectively, of total commercial sales.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited items; the PermeaDerm share is inconsistent across sources
business_model.claim: Cohealyx is made by Regenity and PermeaDerm is licensed from Stedical, and the company keeps only a share of their sale prices, which lowers overall gross margin.
quotes: The Company receives 50% of the average sales price for Cohealyx and up to 55% for PermeaDerm, which lowers the overall gross margin percentage.
Under the terms of the Regenity Agreement, Regenity manufactures and supplies Cohealyx and the Company commercializes it under its private label in the U.S.

business_model.claim: An August amendment with Stedical raised the company's PermeaDerm revenue share to 67% for sheets and 80% for gloves, with a $1.0 million minimum for the year.
quotes: In addition, the Company’s share of revenue from PermeaDerm sales will increase to 67% for products sold in sheet form, subject to increased revenue sharing in the event the Company’s gross margin on those products exceeds 50%, and to 80% for products sold in glove form, subject to increased revenue sharing in the event the Company’s gross margin on those products exceeds 35%.

business_model.claim: The company also manufactures PermeaDerm for Stedical to sell, priced at a ten percent premium to its manufacturing cost.
quotes: The Company will sell PermeaDerm for such sales to Stedical at a ten percent premium to the Company’s actual manufacturing costs.

business_model.claim: Third-quarter gross margin was 84.0%, against 81.3% a year earlier; RECELL alone had a gross margin of 88.4%.
quotes: Gross profit margin across all products was 84.0%, a 270-basis point increase from 81.3% in the same period last year.
The increase in the overall gross margin percentage from the prior year was primarily caused by lower volume discounts, lower inventory reserves

business_model.claim: Revenue depends on hospital reimbursement. When Medicare contractors were slow to publish RECELL payment rates, clinicians used RECELL less.
quotes: In the U.S., RECELL is reimbursed through established inpatient and outpatient reimbursement mechanisms.
Delay by the MACs in establishing and publishing reimbursement rates temporarily slowed clinician use of RECELL.

business_model.claim: A Medicare add-on payment (NTAP) of up to $4,875 per case applied to certain inpatient non-thermal RECELL uses for a limited period.
quotes: This NTAP designation allows Medicare Part A inpatient claims to receive up to $4,875 in additional reimbursement per case, beyond the standard MS-DRG base rate, provided CMS thresholds and coding criteria are met.

business_model.claim: CMS has finalized national physician payment values for RECELL procedures, taking effect next year.
quotes: On November 4, 2026, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services finalized national physician payment values and simplified billing codes for RECELL procedures, effective January 1, 2027

business_model.claim: Weak reimbursement can stop a market: the company paused commercial investment in vitiligo for that reason.
quotes: Despite regulatory approval and demonstrated clinical benefit, reimbursement for vitiligo procedures remains limited and uncertain.
As a result, we have paused further commercial investment in vitiligo at this time.

business_model.claim: Hospital value analysis committees decide whether to adopt the products, and surgeons tend to widen RECELL use from large burns to smaller wounds over time.
quotes: Adoption decisions in burn centers are typically evaluated through hospital value analysis committees (“VACs”), which assess both clinical outcomes and total cost of care.

We have observed that surgeons often adopt RECELL first in larger and more complex burns, where the clinical and economic benefits are most pronounced, and subsequently expand use to smaller or less severe wounds as familiarity with the technology increases.

business_model.claim: Outside the U.S., the company sells partly through third-party distributors.
quotes: We rely on third-party distributors for a portion of our sales in countries outside of the U.S.

business_model.claim: A ten-year BARDA agreement worth up to $25.5 million pays for keeping a RECELL supply ready for mass casualty incidents, including about $4.0 million in access and maintenance fees.
quotes: On April 6, 2026, we entered into a ten-year agreement with the Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority (“BARDA”), part of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, with a total potential value of up to $25.5 million.
The agreement provides approximately $4.0 million in access and maintenance fees over the ten-year term, with additional potential revenue tied to procurement options exercised by BARDA.

business_model.claim: Operating expenses are the largest cost, led by sales and marketing. In the third quarter, sales and marketing was 13,566, G&A 6,307 and R&D 4,697, for total operating expenses of 24,570 (table in thousands).
Sales and marketing cost moves with commissions, incentive pay and the size of the sales force.
quotes: The increase was driven largely by higher sales and marketing expenses, which rose $1.5 million due primarily to increased commissions and compensation, including annual incentive costs.
The decreases are primarily due to the reduction of our sales force as part of cost savings initiatives.

business_model.claim: The company makes RECELL and PermeaDerm at its own Ventura, California facility and buys some components from third-party and single-source suppliers.
quotes: We have a manufacturing facility located in Ventura, California where we produce, package, and warehouse RECELL and PermeaDerm.
